MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 10, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:30 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the tloor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:31 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  1.  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Government Code section
  54956.9(d)(2)
  Development Agreement between the City of Malibu and La Paz Ranch, LLC,
  regarding the property located at 23465 Civic Center Way
  Number of potential cases: (1)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:37 p.m.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of July 10, 2023
  Page 2 of 13

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Director; Richard Mollica, Plarming Director; Susan Dueflas, Public
  Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Christina Munoz, Deputy City
  Clerk; Rob Houston, Interim Deputy City Manager; Loren Davis, Recreation Coordinator;
  Adrianna Fiori, Recreation Coordinator; Chris Orosz, Recreation Supervisor; Kate
  Manisco, Recreation Manager; Amanda Rigali, Recreation Coordinator; and Brittany
  Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Councilmember Riggins led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2), with all Councilmembers present. He stated there was no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettij ohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  30, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Community Services Department Update

  Community Services Director Riesgo, Recreation Manager Manisco, and
  Recreation Supervisor Orosz presented Community Services Department updates.

  The Council expressed its appreciation for the work done by the Community
  Services Department.
   Malibu City Council
  Minut6s of July 10, 2023
  Page 3 of 13

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Kraig Hill stated there were not enough registrations for the adult softball league
  and suggested more outreach by staff. He discussed Senate Bill 423 which allowed
  for easier development of multi-family housing and requested the City work with
  opponents of the bill. He requested Council approve an expense stipend for
  Planning Commissioners and referenced Malibu Municipal Code Section 2.36.1 10.
  He stated that he was told by Council in 201 9 that there was not enough money and
  that the matter would be revisited.

  Ryan Embree discussed the antenna pole in front of Santa Monica College (SMC)
  and stated it violated the City’s conditions of approval. He requested staff provide
  an update at each meeting on the status of the tower. He stated many agreements
  were brought to the Council in June and July and suggested adjustment to the terms
  ofthe contracts, so they were not all due at the same time. He stated that the Consent
  Calendar was not the proper place for contract approval.

  Mario Sandoval, Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA),
  stated presented a video from MRCA on coastal access.

  Jo Drummond thanked the Community Services Department and expressed
  appreciation on behalf ofthe Seawolves Swim Team and the community. She stated
  that she was glad MRCA provided information on public coastal access, but wished
  they maintained their properties better. She indicated support for the Planning
  Commissioner stipend and stated that it might not be needed by some who received
  other perks. She agreed with Mr. Embree about the antenna pole at SMC which
  violated City height and color conditions and needed to be removed. She stated
  variances should not be required for small projects in a landslide area, and did not
  know why they were being required.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary thanked Community Services Department staff for the
  presentation. He announced the July l9, 2023 organic waste recycling virtual
  training and stated that International Plastic Bag Free Day July 3, 2023 kicked off
  the City’s celebration of Plastic Free July. He reported on flre rebuilds and stated
  that 261 permits for single-family dwellings were issued, 131 single-family
  dwellings were complete, 18 multi-family dwelling units were permitted, and 12
  multi-family units were complete. He discussed the July 2, 2023 3.8 magnitude
  offshore earthquake and stated that no damage occurredin Malibu. He stated that
  City staff met with the Bay Foundation and discussed the dune restoration proj ect.
  He provided an update on Assembly Bill 1500 which extended the property tax
  exemption for homes damaged or destroyed by the Woolsey Fire and stated that it
  was moving through the legislature and had not encountered opposition. He stated
  that the State Recycling Association recognized the City as a leader in composting
  and the California Resource Recovery Association honored Malibu with the Dave
  Hardy Leadership Award for organics recycling. He reported staff met with State
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of July 10, 2023
  Page 4 of 13

Parks on the Rindge Dam removal proposal which was in early development stages.
He stated that an update on the Baker Tilly development services review was
forthcoming. He announced the appointment of Alexis Brown as Deputy City
Manager. He announced cancellation of the July 27, 2023 City Council meeting.
He read the City’s statement in response to the Video posted by the MRCA
regarding the removal of unpermitted beach access signs installed on Broad Beach
Road.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, City Manager McClary stated the City was
not contacted by the MRCA before the signs on Broad Beach Road were installed.
He stated that the signs were not removed as agreed by the MRCA after the City
informed them that they were not in compliance with safety standards, and the City
ultimately removed the unpermitted signs.

In response to Councilmember Stewart, City Manager McClary stated he was not
aware of any other unpermitted signs installed by the MRCA and that there were
permitted signs placed by the MRCA in other locations that functioned well.

Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided
crime statistics for 2023 and stated that part one crimes decreased 12.4 percent from
the year prior. He provided a summary of noteworthy arrests which included two
for domestic violence, one residential burglary, eight burglarized vehicles, and
multiple stolen vehicles. He reported activities by special assignment deputies,
which included foot patrols of Legacy Park and Library parking lot, assisting
patrols with calls and traffic stops, and outstanding warrant, parole violation,
suspended license, and failure to register a vehicle instate arrests. He reported an
animal cruelty arrest was made when a dog was discovered without food or water
inside an illegally parked vehicle that was towed to the temporary tow yard.

In response to Councilmember Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund stated that the criminal
case needed to be resolved before it was determined what would happen to the dog,
but in cases of animal cruelty, pets rarely were returned to their owner.

In response to Mayor Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund confirmed that all the type
one crimes he reported were not committed by Malibu residents.

In response to Councilmember Stewart, Sergeant Soderlund stated there were few
maj or incidents over the Independence Day weekend, and most occurred in the late
evening and ovemight hours. He reported there was one hit and run that involved a
motorcyclist that was hit by a truck and the truck’s driver was arrested, and their
vehicle impounded. He commented on a party with 700 attendees that occurred at
Nobu restaurant and stated that the Sheriff Department scheduled a meeting with
Nobu to discuss communication.

Mayor Silverstein commented on the incident with the dog and stated that persons
with mental illness needed better interventions than arrest.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of July 10, 2023
  Page 5 of 13

  Councilmember Grisanti thanked the Sheriff Department for their work over the
  holiday weekend and commented that the individual arrested in connection with the
  dog was on a controlled substance.

  Councilmember Riggins discussed an incident where the Volunteers on Patrol
  (VOP) identified an illegal f1re on Point Dume and recognized their efforts.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Sergeant Soderlund stated that they
  received numerous illegal fireworks calls and identification of involved parties was
  difficult due to other calls they attended. He reported that they were exploring the
  formation of a fireworks suppression unit to target illegal fireworks next year.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring commended the Sheriff Department for their efforts.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, City Manager McClary stated that the party at
  Nobu was unauthorized and unpermitted and enforcement action was pending.

  Councilmember Stewart stated that a party with 700 attendees could not have been
  allowed even with a temporary use permit, considering parking requirements.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated that unpermitted activities had occurred at Nobu for
  many years and solutions proposed were never implemented. He suggested
  measures to restrict unpermitted activity be discussed by the Public Safety
  Commission due to traffic safety concerns.

  Councilmember Riggins indicated agreement with Mayor Pro Tem Uhring and
  added that the fine schedule should be examined and be made more punitive to
  deter the continuation of repeat offenses. She stated that there were complexities
  that might need to involve the Administration and Finance Subcommittee or
  Flaming Commission, and that she looked to the City Manager for a suggested
  course of action.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated that the maj ority of the
  700 attendees used private transportation, but there were party buses, limousines,
  and private coaches parked in the center median of the highway. He stated that the
  response of one deputy was limited in such a situation.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, Interim City Attomey Rusin stated that a
  Code Enforcement action or a specific proj ect could not be addressed by the Public
  Safety Commission but issues that pertained to the public road could. He stated that
  it was a maj or violation of Nobu’s CUP and that it could be examined.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he spent the 4th of July weekend on Arson Watch
  patrol. He stated that everything was quiet until approximately 9:00 p.m. on July
  4th when Broad Beach and Zuma Beach erupted in fireworks and that the response
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of July 10, 2023
  Page 6 of 13

  time was long. He stated that they were fortunate that the weather was damp enough
  that nothing caught fire.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she watched the Point Dume 4th of July parade and
  thanked Pamela Conley Ulich and Paul Major for organizing the parade and
  thanked the VOPs, Sheriff Department, Fire Department, City staff, and all who
  participated. She thanked VOPs, Arson Watch, CERT, and community volunteers
  for their service. She welcomed newly appointed Deputy City Manager Brown.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Planning Director Mollica stated as
  required by the coastal development permit (CDP) for the SMC campus, the County
  applied with the City for required conditional use permit (CUP) for the antennae
  tower. He stated that the application addressed the color and the lighting issues, but
  not the City’s height concerns, so a follow up meeting would be scheduled. He
  stated that the applicant for the County informed the City that it was the County
  counsel’s opinion that they had approval for that height, because that height was
  shown on the project plans that went before the Planning Commission. He
  confirmed that the CUP application would be brought before the Flaming
  Commission at a public hearing.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed the importance of the Point Dume 4th of July
  parade and thanked parade participants and volunteers. He stated that Arson Watch,
  VOPs, CERT, other volunteers, and the Sheriff Department were on duty during
  the holiday weekend and thanked them. ,

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated he did not hear many fireworks near him, but he had
  heard there were unpermitted fireworks on Point Dume into the night and
  questioned why the Fire Department did not respond. He discussed a neighborhood
  in the valley Where the Sheriff’s Department issued individual warnings for
  fireworks in advance of the holiday. He thanked the VOPs for their service and
  discussed their response to recent incidents. He stated that he missed the California
  Strategies meeting that morning and that there was much interest in the community
  about California Senate Bill (SB) 423.

  Mayor Silverstein stated that he attended virtual meetings about public school
  fundraising efforts. He stated that he attended an informational session with Los
  Angeles County Supervisor Lindsay Horvath’s staff. He stated that he attended the
  California Strategies meeting that morning and discussed SB 423. He stated that
  the bill did not have a coastal city exemption and the California Coastal
  Commission was opposed to the bill. He stated that the Council could not act on
  the matter formally, as it was not on the agenda, but they were working with their
  lobbyists to help with the CCC’s obj ections. He discussed drone shows, which were
  an environmentally safe alternative to fireworks displays.

  Recommended Action: Consider the adoption of the attached draft Council
  Interpretation regarding the Council’s interpretation of the use of pesticides
  pursuant  to Local Coastal Program (LCP) Land Use Policy Policy 3.18 as
  “development” in the LCP Local Implementation  Plan.

  Flaming Director Mollica presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Kian Schulman, Joel Schulman, Patt Healy, Doug Carstens, Jo
  Drummond, and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff and Ms. Schulman.

  MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to adopt
  a Local Coastal Program Interpretation regarding the Council’ s interpretation ofthe
  use of pesticides pursuant to Local Coastal Program (LCP) Land Use Policy Policy
  3.18 as “development” in the LCP Local Implementation Plan.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to: 1) delete the Issue section; and 2) amend the
  Interpretation section to read: “The outdoor use of pesticides, including
  insecticides, herbicides, rodenticides or any other similar toxic chemical substance
  is “development” as used in LIP Section 13.3 where the application of such
  substances would have the potential to significantly degrade Environmentally
  Sensitve
  i Habitat Areas (ESHA) or coastal water quality or harm wildlife. Such
  development is also not considered to be “maintenance” under LIP Section 13.4.2
  and therefore, a Coastal Development Permit is required prior to such use.”

  The amendment was accepted by the seconder of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff.

l  FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to add a note that the interpretation was adopted by the
  City Council on July 10, 2023.

  The amendment was accepted by the seconder of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS

  Update Regarding Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 21-002 (Malibu Middle
  and High School Camnus Specific Plan)
  Recommended Action: 1) Receive an update on the Malibu Middle and High
  School (MMHS) Campus Specific Plan; 2) Review the California Coastal
  Commission’s (CCC’s) staff request for a one-year time extension to act on the
  MMHS Campus Specific Plan Local Coastal Program Amendment (LCPA) (LCPA
  No. LCP-4-MAL-22-043-1); and 3) Direct City staff to submit a letter to the CCC
  opposing the one-year extension and for the CCC to direct its staff to prioritize the
  MMHS Campus Specific Plan for consideration during the September 2023 CCC
  hearing.

  Flaming Director Mollica presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for discussion.
MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion to
  authorize the Mayor to submit a letter to the California Coastal Commission (CCC)
  opposing the one-year extension and for the CCC to direct its staff to prioritize the
  MMHS Campus Specific Plan for consideration during the September 2023 CCC
  hearing.
